explanation.headline: Bet 33% was the top play, and you found it.

paragraphs: You held T♦ K♠ in the big blind, against Villain, a LAG player, on the button. Pre-flop, Villain opened to 2.5 bb and you called.
The flop came 3♥ 2♠ 6♠. It was your turn to act with 5 bb in the pot.
sections.title: The hand

paragraphs: You chose Bet 33% (EV 2.29 bb), the top play against Villain's range. Verdict: Best.
Your equity against Villain's whole range is 46.4%.

Bet 33%: Villain folds 34% of the time, more than the 23.1% a bet this size needs to profit on folds alone (1.5 bb / (5 bb + 1.5 bb)), so folds alone pay for it, even when every hand that continues beats you. On top of that, you have 37.1% equity against the hands that continue.
Right now you are ahead of 47.0% of Villain's range. The largest parts of the range are Weak draw (20.6% of it; your equity 61%) and Air (20.6% of it; your equity 80%).
sections.title: The verdict

paragraphs: Villain is a LAG player. Loose-aggressive: wide ranges, frequent pressure, more bluffs.
Villain's range narrowed with each action: Pre-flop: opens to 2.5 bb.
The range in the Range tab is the range this puzzle was graded on.
sections.title: Villain

grade.intent_flag: You labelled this a value bet, but better hands usually continue, though you still have real equity, so it's a semi-bluff.

judged_on_range_note: Graded against Villain's whole range, not this run-out.

simplifications.text: After Hero checks, Villain's bet and Hero's response are simplified: on the river Hero only folds or calls; before the river Villain's bet behind is not modelled.
Before the river, Hero is assumed to realise a share of equity set by position: in position 100%; out of position 80% pre-flop, 88% on the flop, 94% on the turn. All-in pots realise 100%.
After a Villain re-raise, Hero only folds or calls.
